newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia students end 106-day protest, rector resigns.
newsitem.headline: Serbia students end 106-day protest, rector resigns.

text.p: Belgrade students ended their 106-day protest campaign on Friday as their rector resigned to appease them, but new efforts by the ruling Socialists to control the media threatened to provoke fresh unrest.
"Now that my demand for the students to return to classes has been fulfilled... I am tendering my resignation," Belgrade University rector Dragutin Velickovic rector told state media.
Students on Wednesday offered to end their marathon protest and return to classes on Friday if Velickovic stepped down. The rector had said he would resign only when students returned to classes.

University deans loyal to the students pressed them on Wednesday to test Velickovic's promise by returning to their faculties, apparently mindful of a stern warning by the Serbian government that it would cut off the university's funding unless classes resumed.
The student protests had continued even after an opposition coalition ended three months of mass demonstrations in February.
The students carried on marching for press freedom and demanding the resignation of the rector, a diehard Socialist appointee who had condemned the demonstrations.
Velickovic's resignation on Friday took most students by surprise.
"I am very surprised and did not expect such an action, a moral act by a man who had not acted very morally in the past months," Cedomir Antic, a student organizer, told Reuters.
Velickovic had asked for the dismissal of faculty deans and institute chiefs who supported the daily student protest and voted for Velickovic's sacking last Sunday.
